content.user_title: Debug Bugs with Root Cause Discipline
content.value_statement: Bugs often get worse when teams guess at fixes before understanding the failure. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured debugging process.
actual_capabilities: Enforces root cause investigation before suggesting fixes.
Guides reproduction, error reading, recent-change review, and evidence gathering.
Provides a four-phase debugging workflow from investigation to implementation.
Defines rules for testing one hypothesis at a time.
Identifies common shortcuts that lead to repeated failed fixes.
Connects debugging with related testing and tracing skills.
limitations: It is a process guide, not an automated debugger.
It depends on the user providing logs, errors, code, and test results.
It can slow very small fixes when the cause is already proven.
Some examples include shell diagnostics that should be redacted before use.

use_cases.title: Investigate Test Failures
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to reproduce a failing test, trace the failure, and avoid random timing changes.

use_cases.title: Handle Production Bugs
use_cases.description: Structure incident debugging so urgent fixes still use evidence and clear hypotheses.

use_cases.title: Review Failed Fix Attempts
use_cases.description: Stop repeated patching after several failed fixes and decide whether architecture needs review.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Debugging Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use systematic debugging for this issue. First summarize the error, reproduction steps, and evidence we need before any fix.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Test Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the four debugging phases to this failing test. Identify the likely source of the bad state before suggesting code changes.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Competing Hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: List the plausible root causes for this bug, choose one testable hypothesis, and propose the smallest experiment to confirm it.

prompt_templates.title: Recover from Failed Fixes
prompt_templates.prompt: We have tried three fixes and the issue remains. Reassess the evidence, identify architectural risks, and recommend the next investigation step.

output_examples.input: A payment status test sometimes returns pending instead of completed.
output: Restates the observed mismatch and asks for repeatable reproduction steps.
Separates timing symptoms from the actual status update path.
Proposes one experiment that checks where the completed status is lost.

output_examples.input: A production API timeout looks similar to an issue fixed last week.
output: Reads the current error before assuming the old fix applies.
Checks recent changes and affected dependencies.
Defines a minimal mitigation only after evidence supports the cause.

output_examples.input: A previous fix failed and a second quick patch is tempting.
output: Stops additional patching until the failed hypothesis is recorded.
Uses the new evidence to form a different hypothesis.
Escalates to architecture review if repeated fixes reveal deeper coupling.

best_practices: Collect error messages, reproduction steps, and recent changes before proposing fixes.
Test one hypothesis at a time with the smallest useful experiment.
Create or update a failing test before implementing the final fix.
anti_patterns: Adding delays, retries, or broad guards without proving the root cause.
Bundling several fixes together and losing the ability to isolate the result.
Continuing to patch after repeated failed fixes without questioning the design.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code debug technical issues through evidence, hypotheses, tests, and focused fixes.

faq.question: Does it write code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the investigation and only supports implementation after the root cause is understood.

faq.question: Can it be used during incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure urgent debugging, but teams must still choose safe mitigations for live systems.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the error text, reproduction steps, recent changes, affected files, logs, and any failed fixes.

faq.question: Does it replace testing practices?
faq.answer: No. It complements testing by requiring a failing test or clear verification before the final fix.

faq.question: What should I avoid when using it?
faq.answer: Avoid skipping investigation, making multiple changes at once, or logging sensitive environment data during diagnostics.
